A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DiffGAD and contain readable methods, equations, experiments, figures, tables, and Appendices A–D. Corresponding material can be matched despite additions, relocation, and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original DiffGAD benchmark results, component and parameter ablations, representation visualizations, and runtime and memory measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds backbone comparisons and dataset analyses in Appendix C.

M1.justification: Section 3.3 replaces v1's additive corruption through Eq. 3 with z_t=(t/T)z_0+((T-t)/T)epsilon in new Eq. 8. This changes the stated sampling rule while retaining the architecture, losses, and guidance mechanism. However, Algorithm 1 still cites Eq. 3, leaving the implemented rule uncertain.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same node-level anomaly-detection task on Weibo, Reddit, Disney, Books, Enron, and Dgraph, alongside the same synthetic efficiency benchmarks. The new backbone analyses reuse five existing datasets.

E2.justification: The main 13-baseline comparison remains unchanged. Appendix C.5 adds a separate comparison of standalone MLP, VAE, VGAE, and graph-transformer backbones against their DiffGAD counterparts, alongside the existing GAE configuration (Tables 11–12).

E3.justification: v2 adds an evaluation design varying encoder/decoder architectures on five datasets using ROC-AUC, plus analyses measuring neighborhood similarity, clustering coefficients, and anomaly homophily/heterophily. Existing benchmark metrics, training budgets, and tabulated hyperparameters remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix C substantially expands supplementary analysis: C.5 tests backbone dependence, C.6 examines anomaly heterophily in relation to guidance-weight selection, and C.1 adds quantitative dataset diagnostics for weaker performance. The original component ablations and guidance-weight/timestep sweeps are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions state a 20-trial mean-and-standard-deviation reporting protocol. The new backbone tables follow the existing reporting convention, without introducing new seed information, uncertainty procedures, or significance tests. The added embedding variances describe representations rather than experimental uncertainty.

E6.justification: Original benchmark, ablation, and efficiency results remain unchanged, but Tables 11–13 add substantial backbone-specific results and anomaly statistics. For example, v2 newly reports Enron ROC-AUC of 81.9±5.2 for DiffGAD(MLP). It also adds Weibo neighborhood statistics and Books embedding variances. These are additional findings under new configurations or analyses, not same-setting performance improvements.

T1.justification: New Eq. 8 introduces a mathematical corruption definition that is not equivalent to the additive Eq. 3 used by v1's content-preservation procedure. The remaining SDE formulation, objectives, and complexity derivations are retained; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contributions, and conclusion retain the same central claims: direct diffusion-based graph anomaly detection, discriminative-content distillation, general-content preservation, and effectiveness and efficiency across six datasets.

C2.justification: New Appendix C.1 explains dataset-specific weaknesses, including possible overfitting on Disney. C.5 discusses architecture dependence and potentially harmful structural information, while C.6 links guidance strength to anomaly heterophily. These substantially expand applicability and mechanism interpretations, although the Enron heterophily explanation contradicts Table 13.

D1.justification: The advertised repository destination changes from LJH_DiffGAD to DiffGAD, and Appendix C.6 adds guidance-weight selection advice. Software versions, hardware, architecture details, and numerical hyperparameters remain unchanged; v1's hyperparameter Table 11 becomes v2's Table 14.

R1.justification: v2 removes citations including GAD-NR, RenderDiffusion, and MultiDiffusion, and adds Lu et al. (2023, 2024, 2025) and Mao et al. (2025). The substantive positioning relative to diffusion-based generation approaches such as GODM and Diga remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized prose revisions, adds introductory signposting and appendix subsections, shortens the ethics and limitations passages, and adds acknowledgements. Author affiliations and the publication header are updated. The main section sequence and most existing prose are preserved.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 11–13 and an annotated redisplay of the Books visualization as Figure 8. Figure 6 gains variance information, Figure 5 moves earlier, and subsequent figures and the hyperparameter table are renumbered. Table formatting and page arrangement change locally; existing visual analyses are largely retained.

improvement.justification: The new backbone controls and dataset-specific analyses provide useful evidence beyond v1. However, new Eq. 8 contradicts both Eq. 3 retained in Algorithm 1 and the stated small-t behavior. Appendix C.6 also describes Enron as highly heterophilic while Table 13 reports heterophily of 0.00. These additions create material problems in method specification and interpretation alongside the empirical benefits, preventing a reliable judgment of net overall improvement.
